x: There was also a Junior match between the same clubs and in this we had Frank Kemp winning the 100 with John Benstead taking the 220 yards, while Geoff Goode was second to a very promising local youngster in the 1 mile.

Gregory won the 2 miles walk in 14 min. 12.4 secs., and this was our only other success except that our Junior team of Frank Kemp, Alan Law, Ian Forrester and John Benstead won the 4 x 110 yards Junior relay, beating Poly H. and the R.A.F., Halton, in 45.2 secs.
J. Benstead ran in a special 100 yds. handicap, which was put on for the benefit of Treloar, the Australian Olympic runner, and he did well to finish second to the flyer from "down under."
The 100 yards junior final resulted in a win for Alan Law with Frank Kemp second and J.
Jones, our strapping youth, in second place. J. Benstead was second in the 220 yds. and Frank Kemp occupied a similar position in the 440.
Jack Brown 2nd in the Civil Service 1 mile with Bob Taylor 3rd in the 880 yards. J.
The 120 yards Club handicap saw three heats, and those qualifying for the final were : R. Morrell (10), J.

The 300 yards 1st string event was won by Dicky Bartlett in 35.4 secs., and John Benstead won the second race in 34.5. Ian Badiali was first home in the 1st string 660 yards in 87.4 secs., and Bob Taylor recorded 86.5, to set up a new track record in the second race over this distance.
In the Senior events, Dickey Barlett was 2nd, with John Benstead 3rd in the 220, with Alan Law 2nd in the Weight, and Len Bishop was 3rd in the 880 yds.
This was a triangular match, with Queens Park H., Ealing H., and ourselves, and in the 100 yards Senior we had J.

Gordon 2nd, and John Benstead won the 220, with Dicky Bartlett in 3rd place. Dicky also won the 440 yds., beating Ian Badiali, and Jim Heathfield was 3rd in the 880, with Don Maclean 2nd in the 1 mile in 4 mins. 26.9 secs.
On June 3rd we sent a team to Morden for a 4 x 176 yds. relay, and on a rough track our team of Ron Holtum, John Benstead, Ron Morrell and Dudley Gordon ran out winners of a close race.
Inter-Club, Basil Walden and John Benstead both qualified for the final, in which Basil was 1st and John 3rd, which put us well ahead on points.
Jones off 7 yds., with J. Benstead (4) second and Ron Morrell (8) in third place.
Denis Merrett reversed the short sprint result by beating Basil Walden, with J.
The sprinters did well with Basil Walden defeating the holder C. Gibbs, to win the 100 yards, with D Merrett 3rd and J.
